title: Reusing a recovered credential to reach a different principal or host
prerequisites: a credential, key, token or hash recovered from the current foothold
a second service, host or account the recovered material might also authenticate to
excerpt: A credential found on one foothold is a hypothesis about a second one, not a second foothold by itself: the same password, key or session token is often reused across services, environments or accounts, but only trying it tells you which. Enumerate what the recovered material could plausibly reach — same host, same realm, same cloud account, a config file naming another target — before spending it, since a reused credential can lock an account or trip an alert. The effect worth proving is an authenticated session on the new principal through the recovered material, observed from that principal's own response, not the recovery of the material itself.
